documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

28F, financial analyst, moved up from the South in October for a job. Here to establish primary care and get connected with a local MS neurologist.

Neuro history (her account; records requested): In December 2019 she lost vision in the right eye over a few days with pain on moving the eye. Optic neuritis; MRI brain showed white matter lesions and she was told she had relapsing-remitting MS in January 2020. Started interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC three times a week in February 2020 and has stayed on it. Second optic neuritis, this time the left eye, around June 2020. Both eyes recovered to her satisfaction. No other attacks she knows of. Injections go fine, rotates sites, takes them at night.

Bladder: urgency since early 2020. Prior neurologist called it a neurogenic (overactive) bladder from the MS. Oxybutynin 5 mg, uses it some days, maybe 3-4 times a week, usually before long meetings. No leakage, no infections.

PMH otherwise: rheumatic fever as a kid per her mother, she does not know details; never told she had a heart problem from it, no antibiotic prophylaxis.
PSH: none.
Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism on thyroid replacement; father with hypertension. Nobody in the family with MS.
SH: lives alone in an apartment in town. Analyst at a regional firm, hybrid schedule. Never smoked. Wine or a beer once or twice a week. No other substances. Walks most days.
Gyn: last Pap 2019 at her old practice, normal per her.

ROS: no current visual change, numbness, weakness or balance trouble. Mood fine, settling in. Otherwise negative.

EXAM
Vitals as charted. Well appearing.
HEENT: PERRL, no afferent defect today, EOM full without pain. Fundi not well seen without dilation.
Neck supple, no thyromegaly.
Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abd soft, NT, no suprapubic tenderness.
Neuro: CN II-XII grossly intact. Strength 5/5 throughout. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Sensation intact to light touch. Gait normal, tandem ok.
Skin: injection sites on abdomen and thighs without induration.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. Relapsing-remitting MS, on interferon beta-1a, last relapse ~5 months ago. Needs a local MS neurologist; referral placed. Baseline CBC with diff and CMP today (interferon labs), TSH as well given family thyroid disease. Records request to old neurology for MRI and notes.
2. Neurogenic bladder, urgency only, managed with PRN oxybutynin. Continue.
3. History of bilateral optic neuritis, recovered.
4. Childhood rheumatic fever by history, no known cardiac involvement. Normal heart exam.
5. Health maintenance: flu vaccine today. HIV and hep C screening offered, she agreed. Lipids with today's draw. Pap due 2022 based on 2019 result, will confirm once records arrive.

Follow up after neurology sees her, sooner if any new symptoms.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - MS CLINIC
Date of visit: 02/23/2021
Referring: primary care

Thank you for sending Ms. Simard, a 28-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis who is transferring care after moving to the area.

Her illness began with right optic neuritis in late 2019, diagnosed as RRMS in January 2020 on the basis of the MRI findings, followed by left optic neuritis in mid-2020. She has been on interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneously three times weekly since February 2020 and tolerates it without complaint. No new symptoms since the summer. Bladder urgency managed with oxybutynin as needed.

Medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily as needed.
Allergies: none known.

Examination: Alert, fluent. Visual acuity grossly normal both eyes, pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect, fields full to confrontation. Extraocular movements full. Face symmetric. Strength full in all four limbs, tone normal, reflexes symmetric, plantar responses flexor. Sensation intact to all modalities. Coordination and gait normal, tandem intact.

Impression: RRMS, clinically stable on interferon beta-1a; no new deficits on examination.

Plan:
- Continue interferon beta-1a at the current dose.
- Monitoring labs (CBC and hepatic panel every 6 months, TSH yearly) may be drawn through her PCP; please forward results.
- Prescriptions for interferon will continue through our office and the specialty pharmacy.
- Return as needed for new symptoms; she has our nurse line.

Neurology, MS clinic

- Neurogenic bladder: continue oxybutynin; refill sent, 90 days with 3 refills.

Since last year: no new neuro symptoms. Interferon three nights a week. Bladder unchanged, urgency only, no leakage, no UTIs ever. Busy season at work. No new meds.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted to ask about something that's been going on since around September. My left arm and left leg go numb and tingly on and off, sometimes for a few hours. A few times my right eye has gotten blurry and then it clears up by itself after a while. It's not getting worse exactly but it's not going away either and I'm worried it's the MS. Should I see you or neurology?

documents.title: RE: Numb arm and leg
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good morning Samantha. I'm glad you wrote. With your history this needs your neurologist, and they'll likely want a new MRI. I'm messaging the MS clinic this morning to ask for the earliest appointment. If you get sudden vision loss, weakness, or trouble walking or speaking before then, go to the emergency department. Our nurse will call you once we hear back.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST
Indication: multiple sclerosis, intermittent left-sided sensory symptoms and right visual blurring.
Technique: multiplanar multisequence imaging of the brain before and after intravenous gadolinium.
Findings: Multiple ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular white matter bilaterally. No mass effect. Ventricles and sulci normal in size for age. No acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No hemorrhage. Orbits and visualized sinuses unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multiple periventricular white matter lesions in this patient with known multiple sclerosis.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - MS CLINIC
Date of visit: 12/29/2022

Reason for visit: early return for new symptoms, at the PCP's request.

Ms. Simard is a 30-year-old with relapsing-remitting MS on interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC three times weekly. Over roughly the last three months she has had recurring spells of numbness and pins-and-needles in the left arm and left leg, and intermittent blurring of vision in the right eye that clears without treatment. No weakness, no gait change.

Medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Social: relocated from the South about two years ago. Does not smoke.

Exam: Afferent pupillary defect on the right. Reflexes brisk in the left arm and left leg compared with the right. Strength full. Remainder of the exam unchanged.

Data:
- 25-OH vitamin D 15 ng/mL (reference 30-100), low.
- CBC, ESR and CRP normal. ANA negative.
- MRI brain with and without contrast (12/27): multiple periventricular white matter lesions.

Impression: RRMS with a mild relapse, left-sided sensory symptoms and right optic nerve involvement; corresponding exam findings. Vitamin D deficiency.

Plan:
1. Continue interferon beta-1a.
2. Start vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
3. Return as needed for new or worsening symptoms.

Neurology, MS clinic

MRI BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST
Indication: known MS, new left visual blurring.

documents.title: Neurology urgent visit
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - MS CLINIC (urgent slot)
Date of visit: 01/01/2024

Ms. Simard, 31, RRMS on interferon beta-1a, was seen urgently after calling our after-hours line. One year after her last relapse (left-sided sensory symptoms and right visual blurring), she now has two days of blurred vision in the left eye, an electric sensation running down her spine whenever she flexes her neck, and on-and-off numbness and tingling in the right hand for about a month.

Medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Left afferent pupillary defect. Visual acuity reduced on the left. Light-touch sensation diminished in the right hand. Strength, coordination, reflexes and gait otherwise as before; the remainder of the neurologic exam is normal.

Labs: CBC normal, ESR normal, B12 normal, RPR non-reactive, ANA negative.
MRI brain with and without gadolinium: multiple periventricular white matter lesions, a number of them enhancing.

Impression: Relapse of RRMS with left optic neuritis, Lhermitte phenomenon and right-hand sensory symptoms, with active lesions on MRI.

Plan: Continue interferon beta-1a. Return visit in clinic in about 6 months, earlier for any worsening of vision or new deficits.

Neurology, MS clinic

Two relapses this year (left optic neuritis January, right optic neuritis June), both followed by the MS clinic, on interferon throughout. Vision has come back well enough to drive and work.

Main issue today is the bladder. Over the last few months the urgency hits faster and she has started leaking before she gets to the bathroom, a few times a week. Wearing a pad now. Plans errands around restrooms. Takes oxybutynin twice a day most days, not enough. No dysuria, no fever, no hematuria.

ROS otherwise negative. Mood fine, PHQ-9 3.

1. Neurogenic bladder with worsening urgency and new urge leakage despite oxybutynin. Referral to urology for evaluation.
2. RRMS, relapses 1/2024 and 6/2024, per neurology. CBC, CMP, TSH today.
3. Vitamin D deficiency, on D3.
4. Vaccines: flu and 2024-25 COVID today. Pap 2027.
Follow-up after urology.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY PRACTICE
Date of visit: 01/06/2025
Referred by: primary care, for neurogenic bladder with increasing leakage

HPI: 32-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting MS (neurology following) and known neurogenic bladder with detrusor overactivity. Her leakage has become more frequent: the loss of urine comes on abruptly with little warning, sometimes before she can get to a toilet, preceded by a rapidly building urge she cannot hold off. She has become reluctant to be away from home for long stretches. Oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily as needed gives partial relief.
Neurologic history per patient and records: several relapses with visual and sensory symptoms; brain MRIs with multiple lesions.

Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: none.
PSH: none.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks weekly, financial analyst.

Exam: Abdomen soft, no masses. Pelvic exam without masses. Lower extremities with increased tone, brisk reflexes, and reduced joint-position sense at the toes bilaterally.
Post-void residual by bladder scan: 180 mL.

Assessment: Urge urinary incontinence from neurogenic detrusor overactivity, with incomplete emptying (PVR 180 mL), in the setting of MS. Upper motor neuron signs in the legs.

Plan:
1. Clean intermittent catheterization twice daily; teaching done today with our nurse, she performed it independently. Prescription sent to a medical supply company.
2. Continue oxybutynin as currently taken.
3. Follow up in clinic as needed; call for fever or symptoms of infection.

Urology

Meds: interferon beta-1a TIW, oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN, vitamin D3 2000 IU, intermittent catheters. NKDA.

O: T 38.5, BP 120/78, HR 88; rest as charted. Looks tired, not toxic. Abdomen soft and non-tender, no suprapubic tenderness to speak of. No CVA tenderness on either side.
POC urine (cath specimen): LE positive, nitrite positive. Micro: WBC >50/hpf, RBC 2/hpf, many gram-negative rods.
CBC: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250.

A/P
1. Acute cystitis with fever in a woman who self-catheterizes for neurogenic bladder. No flank pain or CVA tenderness. Treating as a complicated course given the fever and catheter use: ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x 7 days. Urine culture sent, will adjust to sensitivities. Fluids, acetaminophen for fever. Clean catheter technique reviewed; new catheter each time.
2. Go to the ED for vomiting, rigors, flank pain or fever that persists past 48 h on the antibiotic.
3. RN call in about 10 days.

Assessment: MS relapse with right optic neuropathy (disc swelling), left arm corticospinal signs, bladder urgency.

Disposition: Discussed with on-call neurology by phone. Discharged home in stable condition with instructions to see her neurologist this week; return for worsening vision, weakness or retention.

CC: legs giving out, numb from the belly button down, cannot urinate.

HPI: 33F with relapsing-remitting MS and neurogenic bladder (self-catheterizes), whose last relapse was right leg weakness in December. Both legs have been getting weaker, she has trouble walking and has fallen several times at home. Numb below the navel. Has not been able to void since this morning. Recalls a right-eye blurring episode about two years ago that cleared on its own.

Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA. FH: mother autoimmune hypothyroidism, father hypertension, no MS.

Exam: Strength 2/5 in both lower extremities. Light touch and pinprick reduced below the T6 level. Lower extremity reflexes brisk. Bilateral upgoing toes.

Workup: CBC normal. ESR normal. B12 normal. Aquaporin-4 IgG negative. Lumbar puncture: CSF oligoclonal bands positive.
MRI spinal cord: T2 hyperintense lesion at T4.

Assessment: Acute myelitis at T4 in known MS, with paraparesis, sensory level and urinary retention.

Disposition: Bladder catheter placed for retention. Admitted to the neurology service.

Emergency medicine

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital neurology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - neurology inpatient service, area hospital
Admitted 06/16/2026 from the ED. Discharged 06/22/2026.

Principal diagnosis: relapse of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis with acute myelitis at T4.

Hospital course: Admitted with bilateral leg weakness (2/5), a T6 sensory level and urinary retention. MRI showed a T2 lesion at T4; AQP4 antibody negative and CSF oligoclonal bands positive, consistent with MS. Treated with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days, tolerated. Indwelling catheter for retention; removed before discharge, and she resumed intermittent self-catheterization without difficulty. Inpatient physical therapy throughout. By discharge leg strength had improved to 4/5 on both sides and she walked the unit with a rolling walker.

Discharge medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC three times weekly (continued until outpatient neurology review); oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily as needed; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Steroid course completed in hospital, no taper.
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home. Rolling walker. Outpatient physical therapy referral placed.

Follow-up: MS clinic within 2-3 weeks to review disease-modifying therapy. Primary care in 1-2 weeks.

Hospital neurology
cc: primary care, MS clinic

Our front desk will call to set it up. Meanwhile, please call or come in for fever, burning with urination, new weakness or a fall.
